title: Entropy increases with dispersal of matter
body: Entropy increases when matter becomes more dispersed, as in solid to liquid or liquid to gas phase changes, or a gas expanding to a larger volume at constant temperature; for reactions involving gas-phase reactants or products, entropy generally increases when the total moles of gas-phase products exceeds the total moles of gas-phase reactants.
caution: The gas-moles rule is only a general trend ("generally"), and it applies to reactions involving gas-phase reactants or products. Argue from the dispersal of the specific particles in the reaction, not from vague "more disorder" wording alone.
ced_evidence: 9.1.A.1 "Entropy increases when matter becomes more dispersed"; "the entropy generally increases when the total number of moles of gas-phase products is greater than the total number of moles of gas-phase reactants"
